title.zh: 卷五 齊本紀下第五 廢帝鬱林王 廢帝海陵恭王 高宗明皇帝 廢帝東昏侯 和帝
title.en: Volume 5 Southern Qi Annals 2: Deposed Emperor Prince of Yulin, Deposed Emperor Prince Gong of Hailing, Emperor Ming, Deposed Emperor Marquess of Donghun, Emperor He
title.raw: 卷五 齊本紀下第五 廢帝鬱林王 廢帝海陵恭王 高宗明皇帝 廢帝東昏侯 和帝 Volume 5 Southern Qi Annals 2: Deposed Emperor Prince of Yulin, Deposed Emperor Prince Gong of Hailing, Emperor Ming, Deposed Emperor Marquess of Donghun, Emperor He

sentences.zh: 廢帝郁林王

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor Prince of Yulin
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor Prince of Yulin

sentences.zh: 廢帝郁林王諱昭業，字元尚，小字法身，文惠太子長子也。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor Prince of Yulin, taboo name Zhaoye, style name Yuanshang, childhood name Fashen, was the eldest son of Crown Prince Wenhu.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor Prince of Yulin, whose taboo name was Zhaoye and style name Yuanshang — childhood name Fashen — was the eldest son of Crown Prince Wenhu.

sentences.zh: 高帝為相王，鎮東府，時年五歲，床前戲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao served as Prince of the Minister, garrisoning the Eastern Headquarters, he was five years old, playing by the bedside.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao was Prince of the Minister and garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, the boy was five and played at the bedside.

sentences.zh: 高帝方令左右拔白髮，問之曰：「兒言我誰耶？

translations.literal: Emperor Gao was having attendants pluck white hairs and asked him, saying, "Child, say — who am I?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao was having attendants pluck out white hairs when he asked the boy, "Tell me — who am I?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「太翁。

translations.literal: " He answered, "Great-grandfather."
translations.idiomatic: "The boy answered, "Great-grandfather."

sentences.zh: 」高帝笑謂左右曰：「豈有為人作曾祖而拔白髮者乎。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gao laughed and said to attendants, "How could one pluck white hairs while serving as someone's great-grandfather?"
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Gao laughed and told his attendants, "Who plucks white hairs for a man acting as someone's great-grandfather?"

sentences.zh: 」即擲鏡、鑷。

translations.literal: " He immediately cast aside mirror and tweezers.
translations.idiomatic: "He at once cast aside mirror and tweezers.

sentences.zh: 其後問訊，高帝指示賓客曰：「我基於此四世矣。

translations.literal: Later at an audience, Emperor Gao pointed him out to guests, saying, "My foundation rests on this one for four generations."
translations.idiomatic: On a later visit, Emperor Gao pointed the boy out to guests and said, "My dynasty's foundation rests on this child — four generations deep."

sentences.zh: 」及武帝即位，封為南郡王，時年十歲。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nan Commandery, aged ten.
translations.idiomatic: "When Emperor Wu took the throne, the boy was enfeoffed as Prince of Nan Commandery at age ten.

sentences.zh: 永明五年十一月戊子，冠於東宮崇正殿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year of Yongming, on wuzi, he was capped in the Eastern Palace's Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifth year of Yongming, on the day wuzi, he received the capping ceremony in the Eastern Palace's Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 其日小會，賜王公以下帛各有差，給南郡王扶二人。

translations.literal: That day a small assembly was held; princes and officials down received silk in graded amounts, and two attendants were granted to the Prince of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That day a small court was held: princes and officials down the ranks received graded gifts of silk, and two attendants were assigned to the Prince of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 七年，有司奏給班劍二十人，鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the relevant offices memorialized granting twenty men with ceremonial swords and one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the relevant offices petitioned to grant him twenty ceremonial sword-bearers and a full band of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 高選友、學，禮絕群王。

translations.literal: Companions and tutors were chosen with the highest care; his ritual treatment surpassed all other princes.
translations.idiomatic: Companions and tutors were chosen with exceptional care, and the ritual honors shown him exceeded those of every other prince.

sentences.zh: 十一年，給皁輪三望車。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, a black-canopied three-canopy carriage was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was granted a black-canopied carriage with three ceremonial canopies.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子薨，立南郡王為皇太孫，居東宮。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhu died, the Prince of Nan Commandery was installed as Imperial Grandson-Heir and dwelt in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Wenhu died, the Prince of Nan Commandery was installed as Imperial Grandson-Heir and took up residence in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 其年七月戊寅，武帝崩，皇太孫即帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: That year, in the seventh month on wuyin, Emperor Wu died; the Imperial Grandson-Heir ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, on wuyin in the seventh month, Emperor Wu died; the Imperial Grandson-Heir took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 八月壬午，詔稱遺詔，以護軍將軍武陵王曄為衛將軍，征南大將軍陳顯達即本號，並開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eighth month on renwu, an edict in the name of the late emperor's testament appointed General Who Protects the Army, Prince of Wuling Ye, as General of the Guard, and Grand General Who Conquers the South Chen Xianda to his existing title, both opening an office with the ceremonial parity of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month on renwu, an edict issued in the name of the late emperor's testament appointed General Who Protects the Army, Prince of Wuling Ye, as General of the Guard, and Grand General Who Conquers the South Chen Xianda retained his existing title — both with offices opening at ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左僕射西昌侯鸞為尚書令，右僕射王晏為左僕射，吏部尚書徐孝嗣為右僕射。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Xichang Luan, was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Right Vice Director Wang Yan was made Left Vice Director; Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Xiaosi was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Xichang Luan, was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing; Right Vice Director Wang Yan became Left Vice Director; and Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Xiaosi became Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 癸未，加司徒竟陵王子良位太傅，增班劍三十人。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Grand Tutor Prince of Jingling Ziliang was promoted to Grand Preceptor and given thirty additional ceremonial sword-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Grand Tutor Prince of Jingling Ziliang was promoted to Grand Preceptor and granted thirty additional ceremonial sword-bearers.

sentences.zh: 蠲除三調及眾逋在今年七月三十日以前者。

translations.literal: The three levies and all overdue taxes owed before the thirtieth day of the seventh month of this year were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: The three levies and all overdue taxes owed before the thirtieth day of the seventh month of that year were remitted.

sentences.zh: 省禦府及無用池田邸冶，減關市徵稅。

translations.literal: Imperial workshops and useless pond-fields and manors in the Directorate of Metallurgy were abolished, and market tolls at passes were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial workshops and unused pond-fields and manors under the Directorate of Metallurgy were abolished, and market tolls at the passes were reduced.

sentences.zh: 先是，每有蠲原之詔，多無事實，督責如故。

translations.literal: Previously, whenever there were edicts remitting or pardoning debts, in fact little was done; supervision and collection continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, whenever edicts remitted or pardoned debts, little actually changed — supervision and collection continued as before.

sentences.zh: 是時西昌侯鸞任知朝政，天下咸望風來蘇，至此恩信兩行，海內莫不欣然。

translations.literal: At this time Marquis of Xichang Luan held actual power over court affairs; all under Heaven looked to him for renewal — here grace and trust both took effect, and within the seas none did not rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Marquis of Xichang Luan held real authority over court affairs; the realm looked to him for renewal — and when grace and trust both took effect, people throughout the empire rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 九月辛酉，追尊文惠皇太子為世宗文皇帝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on xinyou, the late Crown Prince Wenhu was posthumously honored as Emperor Shizong Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month on xinyou, the late Crown Prince Wenhu was posthumously honored as Emperor Shizong Wen.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬寅，尊皇太孫太妃為皇太后，立皇后何氏。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on renyin, the Imperial Grandson-Heir's consort-mother was honored as Empress Dowager, and Empress He was installed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter on renyin, the Imperial Grandson-Heir's consort-mother was honored as Empress Dowager, and Empress He was installed.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚戌，魏人來聘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on gengxu, Wei envoys came on a diplomatic visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month on gengxu, envoys from Wei came on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，立臨汝公昭文為新安王、曲江公昭秀為臨海王，皇弟昭粲為永嘉王。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Duke of Linru Zhaowen was installed as Prince of Xin'an, Duke of Qujiang Zhaoxiu as Prince of Linhai, and the emperor's younger brother Zhaocan as Prince of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Duke of Linru Zhaowen was installed as Prince of Xin'an, Duke of Qujiang Zhaoxiu as Prince of Linhai, and the emperor's younger brother Zhaocan as Prince of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 二月辛卯，祀明堂。

translations.literal: In the second month on xinmao, the Bright Hall was sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month on xinmao, sacrifices were offered at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 閏月丁卯，以鎮軍大將軍西昌侯鸞即本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month on dingmao, Grand General Who Garrisons the Army, Marquis of Xichang Luan, received his existing title with an office opening at ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month on dingmao, Grand General Who Garrisons the Army, Marquis of Xichang Luan, retained his existing title with an office opening at ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 五月甲戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, jiaxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month, jiaxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸巳，皇太后令廢帝為郁林王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on guisi, the Empress Dowager issued an order deposing the emperor as Prince of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn on guisi, the Empress Dowager issued an order deposing the emperor as Prince of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 帝少美容止，好隸書，武帝特所鍾愛，敕皇孫手書不得妄出以貴之。

translations.literal: The emperor from youth had fine appearance and bearing, loved clerical script; Emperor Wu especially cherished him and ordered that the imperial grandson's own handwriting must not be casually sent out, to preserve its value.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the emperor had fine looks and bearing and loved clerical script; Emperor Wu especially doted on him and ordered that the imperial grandson's own handwriting must not be casually circulated, so as to preserve its value.

sentences.zh: 進退音吐，甚有令譽。

translations.literal: In advancing, retreating, speech and tone, he had much fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In how he advanced and retreated, spoke and carried himself, he won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 生而為竟陵文宣王所攝養，常在袁妃間。

translations.literal: From birth he was raised by Prince of Jingling, Duke Wenxuan, and constantly stayed in Lady Yuan's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was raised by Prince of Jingling, Duke Wenxuan, and lived constantly in Lady Yuan's quarters.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王移住西州，帝亦隨住焉。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingling moved to dwell in West Prefecture, the emperor also moved there.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jingling moved to West Prefecture, the emperor moved there as well.

sentences.zh: 性甚辯慧，哀樂過人。

translations.literal: By nature he was very clever and eloquent; joy and grief exceeded ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was very clever and eloquent, and his joy and grief ran deeper than those of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 接對賓客，皆款曲周至。

translations.literal: In receiving and answering guests, all were treated with warm courtesy to the full.
translations.idiomatic: When receiving and answering guests, he treated each with warm, thorough courtesy.

sentences.zh: 矯情飾詐，陰懷鄙慝。

translations.literal: He feigned feeling and adorned deception, secretly harboring base malice.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned feeling and practiced deception while secretly harboring base malice.

sentences.zh: 與左右無賴群小二十許人共衣食，同臥起。

translations.literal: With some twenty-odd worthless petty men at his side he shared food and clothing and slept and rose together.
translations.idiomatic: With some twenty-odd worthless petty men at his side he shared food and clothing, sleeping and rising together.

sentences.zh: 妃何氏擇其中美貌者，皆與交歡。

translations.literal: Consort He selected the handsome among them, and all were given to share her bed.
translations.idiomatic: Consort He selected the handsome among them and took them all to her bed.

sentences.zh: 密就富市人求錢，無敢不與。

translations.literal: Secretly he went to wealthy townspeople to demand money; none dared refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he went to wealthy townspeople to demand money, and none dared refuse.

sentences.zh: 及竟陵王移西邸，帝獨住西州，每夜輒開後堂合，與諸不逞小人，至諸營署中淫宴。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingling moved to the Western Residence, the emperor alone remained in West Prefecture; each night he would open the rear hall doors and, with various unruly petty men, go to various barracks and offices for licentious feasts.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jingling moved to the Western Residence, the emperor alone remained in West Prefecture; each night he opened the rear hall doors and, with various unruly petty men, went to barracks and offices throughout the compound for licentious feasts.

sentences.zh: 凡諸小人，並逆加爵位，皆疏官名號于黃紙，使各囊盛以帶之，許南面之日，即便施行。

translations.literal: All such petty men in turn received ennoblement; their official titles and ranks were written on yellow paper, each kept in a pouch at the belt, with the promise that on the day he faced south as ruler they would at once take effect.
translations.idiomatic: All such petty men in turn received ennoblement; their official titles and ranks were written on yellow paper, each kept in a pouch at the belt, with the promise that on the day he faced south as ruler they would take effect at once.

sentences.zh: 又別作鑰鉤，兼善效人書，每私出還，輒扃鑰，封題如故，故人無知者。

translations.literal: He also made separate key-hooks and was skilled at imitating others' handwriting; whenever he went out privately and returned, he would lock and seal as before, so people knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He also made separate key-hooks and was skilled at imitating others' handwriting; whenever he went out privately and returned, he locked and sealed everything as before, so no one knew.

sentences.zh: 師史仁祖、侍書胡天翼聞之，相與謀曰：「若言之二宮，則其事未易，若于營署為異人所毆打，及犬物所傷，豈直罪止一身，亦當盡室及禍。

translations.literal: Mentor Shi Renzu and Attendant Scribe Hu Tianyi heard of it and together plotted, saying, "If we report it to the two palaces, the matter will not be easy; if at a barracks or office we are beaten by strangers, or injured by dogs or things, the crime will not stop at one person — the whole household will suffer disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Mentor Shi Renzu and Attendant Scribe Hu Tianyi heard of it and plotted together: "If we report it to the two palaces, the matter will not be easy to manage; if at a barracks or office we are beaten by strangers, or injured by dogs or other things, the crime will not stop with us — our whole households will be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 年各已七十，餘生寧足吝邪。

translations.literal: Each is already seventy; what remains of life — is it worth sparing?
translations.idiomatic: Each of us is already seventy — what remains of life is hardly worth clinging to.

sentences.zh: 」數日中，二人相系自殺，二宮不知也。

translations.literal: " Within several days the two men hanged themselves in succession; the two palaces did not know.
translations.idiomatic: "Within several days the two men hanged themselves in succession; the two palaces knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 武帝以暨陽縣寒人給事中綦母珍之代仁祖，剡縣寒人馬澄代天翼。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu replaced Renzu with Qimu Zhenzhi of Jiyang County, a poor man serving as Attendant at the Palace, and Tianyi with Ma Cheng of Shan County, also a poor man.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu replaced Renzu with Qimu Zhenzhi of Jiyang County, a poor man serving as Attendant at the Palace, and Tianyi with Ma Cheng of Shan County, likewise a poor man.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子每禁其起居，節其用度。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhu constantly restricted his comings and goings and curtailed his expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhu constantly restricted his comings and goings and curtailed his expenses.

sentences.zh: 帝謂豫章王妃庾氏曰：「阿婆，佛法言有福生帝王家，今見作天王，便是大罪，左右主帥，動見拘執，不如市邊屠酤富兒百倍。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Consort of Yuzhang, Lady of the Yu clan, "Grandmother, Buddhist teaching says those with fortune are born in an imperial house — now I see being made Son of Heaven is a great crime; the attendants and commanders at my side are constantly seized and restrained — better a hundred times to be a rich butcher or wine-seller at the market edge."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Consort of Yuzhang, Lady Yu, "Grandmother, the Buddhist teaching says the fortunate are born into an imperial house — yet I find that being made Son of Heaven is a great crime; the attendants and commanders at my side are constantly seized and restrained. Better a hundred times over to be a rich butcher or wine-seller at the market edge."

sentences.zh: 文惠太子自疾及薨，帝侍疾及居喪，哀容號毀，旁人見者，莫不嗚咽。

translations.literal: From Crown Prince Wenhu's illness through his death, the emperor attended his sickbed and observed mourning; his grieving countenance and wailing destroyed his appearance — those who saw him nearby all sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: From Crown Prince Wenhu's illness through his death, the emperor attended the sickbed and observed mourning; his grieving face and wailing seemed to destroy him — all who saw him nearby sobbed.

sentences.zh: 裁還私室，即歡笑酣飲，備食甘滋。

translations.literal: Barely back in his private quarters, he at once laughed and drank deeply, with every delicacy prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Barely back in his private quarters, he at once laughed and drank deeply, with every delicacy laid out.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，立為皇太孫。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete, he was installed as Imperial Grandson-Heir.
translations.idiomatic: When the burial was complete, he was installed as Imperial Grandson-Heir.

sentences.zh: 問訊太妃，截壁為合，于太妃房內往何氏間，每入輒彌時不出。

translations.literal: Visiting the Grand Consort, he cut through a wall to make a door and, within the Grand Consort's chambers, went to Lady He's quarters; each entry lasted a long time before he emerged.
translations.idiomatic: When visiting the Grand Consort, he cut through a wall to make a door and, from within her chambers, passed into Lady He's quarters; each visit lasted a long time before he emerged.

sentences.zh: 武帝往東宮，帝迎拜號慟，絕而復蘇，武帝自下輿抱持之，寵愛日隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu came to the Eastern Palace, the emperor came forward bowing and wailing; he fainted and revived — Emperor Wu descended from the carriage to hold him; favor daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu came to the Eastern Palace, the emperor came forward bowing and wailing until he fainted and revived; Emperor Wu descended from the carriage to hold him, and favor toward him daily increased.

sentences.zh: 又在西州令女巫楊氏禱祀，速求天位。

translations.literal: Also while in West Prefecture he ordered the witch Lady Yang to pray and sacrifice, urgently seeking the heavenly throne.
translations.idiomatic: While in West Prefecture he also ordered the witch Lady Yang to pray and sacrifice, urgently seeking the throne.

sentences.zh: 及文惠薨，謂由楊氏之力，倍加敬信，呼楊婆。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhu died, he said it was through Lady Yang's power; he doubled respect and trust and called her Mother Yang.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Wenhu died, he attributed it to Lady Yang's power; he doubled his respect and trust and called her Mother Yang.

sentences.zh: 宋氏以來，人間有楊婆兒哥，蓋此征也。

translations.literal: Since the Song dynasty there had been a folk song about Mother Yang's boy — this was its fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Song dynasty there had been a folk song about Mother Yang's boy — this was its fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 武帝有疾，又令楊氏日夜禱祈，令宮車早晏駕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu fell ill, he again had Lady Yang pray day and night, wishing the imperial carriage would depart early or late.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu fell ill, he again had Lady Yang pray day and night, wishing the imperial carriage would depart sooner rather than later.

sentences.zh: 時何妃在西州，武帝未崩數日，疾稍危，與何氏書，紙中央作一大「喜」字，而作三十六小「喜」字繞之。

translations.literal: At that time Consort He was in West Prefecture; several days before Emperor Wu's death, when the illness grew critical, he wrote to Lady He — in the center of the paper one large character "Joy," surrounded by thirty-six small characters "Joy."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Consort He was in West Prefecture; several days before Emperor Wu's death, as the illness grew critical, he wrote to Lady He — in the center of the paper one large character Joy, surrounded by thirty-six small characters Joy.

sentences.zh: 侍武帝疾，憂容慘戚，言發淚下。

translations.literal: Attending Emperor Wu's illness, his grieving countenance was wretched; words issued and tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: While attending Emperor Wu's illness, his grieving face was wretched; he spoke and wept by turns.

sentences.zh: 武帝每言及存亡，帝輒哽咽不自勝。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Wu spoke of life and death, the emperor would choke and be unable to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Wu spoke of life and death, the emperor choked with grief and could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 武帝以此謂為必能負荷大業，謂曰：「五年中一委宰相，汝勿厝意。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu therefore thought he would surely be able to bear the great enterprise and told him, "For five years entrust all to the chief minister — do not concern yourself."
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Wu therefore believed he would surely bear the great enterprise and told him, "For five years entrust everything to the chief minister — do not concern yourself."

sentences.zh: 五年以後，勿復委人。

translations.literal: After five years, do not again entrust to others.
translations.idiomatic: After five years, do not again entrust power to others.

sentences.zh: 若自作無成，無所多恨。

translations.literal: If you yourself achieve nothing, there is not much to regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you yourself achieve nothing, there will not be much to regret.

sentences.zh: 」臨崩，執帝手曰：「阿奴，若憶翁，當好作。

translations.literal: " At the point of death, he grasped the emperor's hand and said, "Little one, if you remember old grandfather, you must do well."
translations.idiomatic: "At the point of death he grasped the emperor's hand and said, "Little one, if you remember old grandfather, you must do well."

sentences.zh: 」如此再而崩。

translations.literal: " Thus twice, then he died.
translations.idiomatic: "He said this twice, then died.

sentences.zh: 大斂始畢，乃悉呼武帝諸伎，備奏眾樂，諸伎雖畏威從事，莫不哽咽流涕。

translations.literal: When the great encoffining was just complete, he summoned all Emperor Wu's performers and had every kind of music played; though the performers feared authority and complied, none did not choke and weep.
translations.idiomatic: When the great encoffining was just complete, he summoned all Emperor Wu's performers and had every kind of music played; though the performers feared authority and complied, all choked back tears.

sentences.zh: 素好狗馬，即位未逾旬，便毀武帝所起招婉殿，以材賜閹人徐龍駒，於其處為馬埒。

translations.literal: He had always loved dogs and horses; within ten days of ascending the throne he destroyed the Zhaowan Hall that Emperor Wu had built, giving the timber to the eunuch Xu Longju to make a horse course in that place.
translations.idiomatic: He had always loved dogs and horses; within ten days of ascending the throne he destroyed the Zhaowan Hall that Emperor Wu had built, giving the timber to the eunuch Xu Longju to make a horse course on the site.

sentences.zh: 馳騎墜馬，面額並傷，稱疾不出者數日。

translations.literal: Galloping he fell from his horse; face and forehead were both injured; he claimed illness and did not go out for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Galloping, he fell from his horse and injured face and forehead; he claimed illness and did not appear for several days.

sentences.zh: 多聚名鷹快犬，以粱肉奉之。

translations.literal: He gathered many famous hawks and swift dogs, feeding them with millet and meat.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered many famous hawks and swift dogs, feeding them millet and meat.

sentences.zh: 及武帝梓宮下渚，帝於端門內奉辭，轀輬車未出端門，便稱疾還內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu's inner coffin descended to the ford, the emperor offered farewell within the Duan Gate; before the wheeled bier had left the Duan Gate, he claimed illness and returned within.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu's inner coffin descended to the ford, the emperor offered farewell within the Duan Gate; before the wheeled bier had left the gate, he claimed illness and returned inside.

sentences.zh: 裁入合，即于內奏胡伎，鞞鐸之聲，震響內外。

translations.literal: Barely entering the private chambers, he at once had barbarian performers play within; the sound of drums and cymbals shook inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Barely inside the private chambers, he at once had barbarian performers play; the sound of drums and cymbals shook the palace inside and out.

sentences.zh: 時司空王敬則問新除射聲校尉蕭坦之曰：「便如此，不當匆匆邪？

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Wang Jingze asked the newly appointed Commandant of Archers Xiao Tanzhi, "To be like this — should it not be hurried?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Minister of Works Wang Jingze asked the newly appointed Commandant of Archers Xiao Tanzhi, "To behave like this — should it not wait a little?"

sentences.zh: 」坦之曰：「此政是內人哭響徹耳。

translations.literal: " Tanzhi said, "This is precisely the sound of the inner quarters weeping reaching the ears."
translations.idiomatic: "Tanzhi said, "That is simply the sound of the inner quarters weeping, reaching our ears."

sentences.zh: 」自山陵之後，便於合內乘內人車問訊，往皇后所生母宋氏間，因微服遊走市里。

translations.literal: After the mountain tomb, he would ride inner-quarters carriages to pay visits, going to the empress's birth-mother Lady Song's quarters, and also went in plain dress wandering the market streets.
translations.idiomatic: After the mountain tomb, he rode inner-quarters carriages to pay visits, going to the empress's birth-mother Lady Song's quarters, and also went in plain dress wandering the market streets.

sentences.zh: 又多往文帝崇安陵隧中，與群小共作諸鄙褻擲塗賭跳、放鷹走狗雜狡獪。

translations.literal: He also often went to Emperor Wen's Chong'an Tomb tunnel, with petty men together performing various vulgar obscenities — smearing and gambling, leaping, releasing hawks and running dogs, and assorted roguery.
translations.idiomatic: He also often went to Emperor Wen's Chong'an Tomb tunnel, where with petty men he performed every vulgar obscenity — smearing, gambling, leaping, releasing hawks and running dogs, and assorted roguery.

sentences.zh: 帝既失道，朝事大小，皆決之西昌侯鸞，鸞有諫，多不見從。

translations.literal: The emperor having lost the Way, great and small court affairs were all decided by Marquis of Xichang Luan; when Luan remonstrated, much was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor having lost the Way, great and small court affairs were all decided by Marquis of Xichang Luan; when Luan remonstrated, his advice was often ignored.

sentences.zh: 極意賞賜左右，動至百數十萬。

translations.literal: He bestowed rewards on attendants to the utmost — often reaching hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed rewards on attendants to the utmost — often reaching into the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 每見錢曰：「我昔思汝一個不得，今日得用汝未？

translations.literal: Whenever he saw money he said, "I once longed for you and could not get a single one — today can I use you yet?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw money he said, "I once longed for you and could not get a single coin — today, can I use you at last?"

sentences.zh: 」武帝聚錢上庫五億萬，齋庫亦出三億萬，金銀布帛不可稱計。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had amassed five hundred million in the upper treasury and three hundred million in the fasting treasury; gold, silver, silk and cloth beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had amassed five hundred million in the upper treasury and three hundred million in the fasting treasury; gold, silver, silk and cloth beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 即位未期歲，所用已過半，皆賜與諸不逞群小。

translations.literal: Within less than a year of ascending the throne, more than half had been used — all bestowed on various unruly petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than a year of ascending the throne, more than half had been spent — all bestowed on various unruly petty men.

sentences.zh: 取諸寶器以相擊剖破碎之，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: He took various precious vessels and struck them against each other to break them, taking it as laughter and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He took various precious vessels and struck them against each other to smash them, taking it as laughter and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 及至廢黜，府庫悉空。

translations.literal: By the time of deposition, the storehouses were entirely empty.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of his deposition, the storehouses were entirely empty.

sentences.zh: 其在內，常裸袒，著紅紫錦繡新衣、錦帽、紅縠褌，雜采衵服。

translations.literal: Within the palace he constantly went bare-chested, wearing new red and purple brocade clothes, brocade caps, red gauze drawers, and multicolored undergarments.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace he constantly went bare-chested, wearing new red and purple brocade clothes, brocade caps, red gauze drawers, and multicolored undergarments.

sentences.zh: 好鬥雞，密買雞至數千價。

translations.literal: He loved cockfighting and secretly bought cocks worth thousands each.
translations.idiomatic: He loved cockfighting and secretly bought cocks worth thousands each.

sentences.zh: 武帝御物甘草杖，宮人寸斷用之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's personal licorice staff — palace women cut it inch by inch for use.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's personal licorice staff — palace women cut it inch by inch for their use.

sentences.zh: 徐龍駒為後合舍人，日夜在六宮房內。

translations.literal: Xu Longju served as rear-hall attendant; day and night he was in the six palaces' quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Longju served as rear-hall attendant and day and night remained in the six palaces' quarters.

sentences.zh: 帝與文帝幸姬霍氏淫通，改姓徐氏，龍駒勸長留宮內，聲雲度霍氏為尼，以餘人代之。

translations.literal: The emperor committed adultery with Emperor Wen's favored concubine Lady Huo, changing her surname to Xu; Longju urged keeping her long in the palace, claiming Huo had become a nun and substituting another person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor committed adultery with Emperor Wen's favored concubine Lady Huo, changing her surname to Xu; Longju urged keeping her long in the palace, claiming Huo had become a nun while substituting another person.

sentences.zh: 皇后亦淫亂，齋合通夜洞開，內外淆雜，無復分別。

translations.literal: The empress also was licentious; the fasting chambers' doors stood open all night; inside and outside were confused — no distinction remained.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was also licentious; the fasting chambers' doors stood open all night; inside and outside were confused and no distinction remained.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人綦母珍之、朱隆之，直合將軍曹道剛、周奉叔並為之羽翼。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Qimu Zhenzhi and Zhu Longzhi, Direct Attendant Generals Cao Daogang and Zhou Fengshu all served as his wings.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Qimu Zhenzhi and Zhu Longzhi, Direct Attendant Generals Cao Daogang and Zhou Fengshu all served as his wings.

sentences.zh: 西昌侯鸞屢諫不納；

translations.literal: Marquis of Xichang Luan repeatedly remonstrated without acceptance;
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Xichang Luan repeatedly remonstrated, but his advice was not accepted;

sentences.zh: 既而尼媼外入，頗傳異語，乃疑鸞有異志。

translations.literal: Then nuns and old women from outside entered and spread strange talk — he therefore suspected Luan of disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Then nuns and old women from outside entered and spread strange talk — he therefore suspected Luan of disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 中書令何胤以皇后從叔見親，使直殿省。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat He Yin, as the empress's maternal uncle, was treated as kin and made to attend the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Secretariat He Yin, as the empress's maternal uncle, was treated as kin and made to attend the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 常隨後呼胤為三父。

translations.literal: He constantly followed behind calling Yin "Third Father."
translations.idiomatic: He constantly followed behind calling Yin "Third Father."

sentences.zh: 與胤謀誅鸞，令胤受事，胤不敢當，依違杜諫，乃止。

translations.literal: With Yin he plotted to execute Luan, ordering Yin to take charge of affairs; Yin dared not accept and evasively remonstrated — then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With Yin he plotted to execute Luan, ordering Yin to take charge of affairs; Yin dared not accept and evasively remonstrated — then the plan stopped.

sentences.zh: 又謀出鸞於西州，中敕用事，不復關諮。

translations.literal: He again plotted to send Luan out to West Prefecture and handle affairs by inner edict without further consultation.
translations.idiomatic: He again plotted to send Luan out to West Prefecture and handle affairs by inner edict without further consultation.

sentences.zh: 鸞慮變，先使蕭諶、坦之等於省誅曹道剛、朱隆之等，率兵自尚書省入雲龍門，戎服加朱衣於上。

translations.literal: Luan fearing change, first sent Xiao Chen and Tanzhi and others to execute Cao Daogang, Zhu Longzhi and others at the secretariat, then led troops from the Masters of Writing office into the Cloud Dragon Gate, wearing armor with vermilion robes over it.
translations.idiomatic: Luan, fearing change, first sent Xiao Chen and Tanzhi and others to execute Cao Daogang, Zhu Longzhi and others at the secretariat, then led troops from the Masters of Writing office into the Cloud Dragon Gate, wearing armor with vermilion robes over it.

sentences.zh: 比入門，三失履，王晏、徐孝嗣、蕭坦之、陳顯達、王廣之、沈文季系進。

translations.literal: Just entering the gate, thrice he lost his shoes; Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Xiao Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi and Shen Wenji followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Just entering the gate, thrice he lost his shoes; Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Xiao Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi and Shen Wenji followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 帝在壽昌殿，裸身與霍氏相對，聞外有變，使閉內殿諸房合，令閹人登興光樓望，還報云：「見一人戎服，從數百人，急裝，在西鐘樓下。

translations.literal: The emperor was in Shouchang Hall, naked facing Lady Huo; hearing disturbance outside, he ordered the inner hall rooms closed; he sent a eunuch to ascend Xingguang Tower to look, reporting, "I see one man in armor with several hundred men, urgently equipped, at the west bell tower."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in Shouchang Hall, naked facing Lady Huo; hearing disturbance outside, he ordered the inner hall rooms closed and sent a eunuch to ascend Xingguang Tower to look; the report came, "I see one man in armor with several hundred men, urgently equipped, at the west bell tower."

sentences.zh: 」須臾，蕭諶領兵先入宮，帝走向愛姬徐氏房，拔劍自刺不入，以帛纏頸，輿接出延德殿。

translations.literal: " In a moment Xiao Chen led troops first into the palace; the emperor ran toward favored concubine Lady Xu's room, drew a sword and stabbed himself without penetrating, wrapped cloth around his neck, and was carried out in a litter to Yande Hall.
translations.idiomatic: "In a moment Xiao Chen led troops first into the palace; the emperor ran toward favored concubine Lady Xu's room, drew a sword and stabbed himself without penetrating, wrapped cloth around his neck, and was carried out in a litter to Yande Hall.

sentences.zh: 諶初入殿，宿衛將士皆執弓楯欲戰，諶曰：「所取自有人，卿等不須動。

translations.literal: When Chen first entered the hall, the night-guard soldiers all grasped bows and shields intending to fight; Chen said, "What is taken has its owner — you need not move."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen first entered the hall, the night-guard soldiers all grasped bows and shields intending to fight; Chen said, "What is taken has its owner — you need not move."

sentences.zh: 」宿衛信之。

translations.literal: The night-guard believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The night-guard believed him.

sentences.zh: 及帝出，各欲自奮，帝竟無一言。

translations.literal: When the emperor came out, each wished to exert himself — the emperor ultimately said not a word.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came out, each soldier wished to fight — the emperor ultimately said not a word.

sentences.zh: 出西弄，遇弑，年二十二。

translations.literal: Exiting the western lane, he encountered assassination, aged twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Exiting the western lane, he was assassinated, aged twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 舁屍出徐龍駒宅，殯葬以王禮。

translations.literal: The corpse was carried out to Xu Longju's residence and buried with princely rites.
translations.idiomatic: The corpse was carried out to Xu Longju's residence and buried with princely rites.

sentences.zh: 霍氏及廣昌君宋並賜死，餘黨亦見誅。

translations.literal: Lady Huo and Guangchang Lord Song were both ordered to die; the remaining partisans were also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huo and Guangchang Lord Song were both ordered to die; the remaining partisans were also executed.

sentences.zh: 先是文惠太子立樓館於鍾山下，號曰：「東田」，太子屢游幸之，「東田」反語為「顛童」也。

translations.literal: Previously Crown Prince Wenhu had built a tower pavilion at Zhong Mountain called "Eastern Field"; the crown prince often toured there — "Eastern Field" reversed is "mad boy."
translations.idiomatic: Previously Crown Prince Wenhu had built a tower pavilion at Zhong Mountain called Eastern Field; the crown prince often toured there — Eastern Field reversed reads as mad boy.

sentences.zh: 武帝又於青溪立宮，號曰：「舊宮」，反之「窮廄」也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also built a palace at Qing Stream called "Old Palace" — reversed, "ruined stable."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu also built a palace at Qing Stream called Old Palace — reversed, it reads ruined stable.

sentences.zh: 果以輕狷而至於窮。

translations.literal: In the end through frivolity he came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, through frivolity, he came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 又武帝時有小史姓皇名太子，武帝曰：「皇太子非名之謂」，於是移點于外，易名為犬子。

translations.literal: Also in Emperor Wu's time there was a petty clerk surnamed Huang named Taizi; Emperor Wu said, "Imperial Grandson-Heir is not a name to be used" — the dot was moved outward and the name changed to Dog-son.
translations.idiomatic: Also in Emperor Wu's time there was a petty clerk surnamed Huang named Taizi; Emperor Wu said, "Imperial Grandson-Heir is not a name to be used" — the dot was moved outward and the name changed to Dog-son.

sentences.zh: 處士何點曰：「太子者，天地之所懸，三才之所系，今化而為犬，不得立矣。

translations.literal: Recluse He Dian said, "The crown prince is what Heaven and Earth suspend, what the Three Powers tie to — now transformed into a dog, he cannot be installed."
translations.idiomatic: Recluse He Dian said, "The crown prince is what Heaven and Earth suspend and the Three Powers tie to — now transformed into a dog, he cannot be installed."

sentences.zh: 」既而文惠太子薨，郁林、海陵相繼廢黜，此其驗也。

translations.literal: " Then Crown Prince Wenhu died; Yulin and Hailing were deposed in succession — this was the verification.
translations.idiomatic: "Then Crown Prince Wenhu died; Yulin and Hailing were deposed in succession — this was the verification.

sentences.zh: 永明中，百姓忽著破後帽，始自建業，流於四遠，貴賤翕然服之，此服祅也。

translations.literal: In Yongming, common people suddenly wore torn-back hats, starting from Jianye and spreading to the four directions; noble and base all suddenly wore them — this clothing was an omen.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming, common people suddenly wore torn-back hats, starting from Jianye and spreading in every direction; noble and base alike suddenly wore them — this clothing was an omen.

sentences.zh: 帽自蕭諶之家，其流遂遠，天意若曰：武穆、文昭皆當滅，而諶亦誅死之效焉。

translations.literal: The hats originated from Xiao Chen's household; the stream then went far — Heaven's intent seemed to say: Wu and Mu and Wen and Zhao should all be destroyed, and Chen's execution was also the effect.
translations.idiomatic: The hats originated from Xiao Chen's household; the fashion then spread far — Heaven's intent seemed to say that Wu and Mu and Wen and Zhao should all be destroyed, and Chen's execution was also foretold.

sentences.zh: 廢帝海陵恭王

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor Prince Gong of Hailing
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor Prince Gong of Hailing

sentences.zh: 廢帝海陵恭王諱昭文，字季尚，文惠太子第二子也。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor Prince Gong of Hailing, taboo name Zhaowen, style name Jishang, was Crown Prince Wenhu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor Prince Gong of Hailing, whose taboo name was Zhaowen and style name Jishang, was Crown Prince Wenhu's second son.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，封臨汝公，郁林王即位，改封新安王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linru; when Prince of Yulin ascended the throne, he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linru; when Prince of Yulin ascended the throne, he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 及郁林廢，西昌侯鸞奉帝纂統。

translations.literal: When Yulin was deposed, Marquis of Xichang Luan installed the emperor to succeed the line.
translations.idiomatic: When Yulin was deposed, Marquis of Xichang Luan installed the emperor to succeed the imperial line.

sentences.zh: 八月壬辰，魏人來聘。

translations.literal: In the eighth month on renchen, Wei envoys came on a diplomatic visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month on renchen, envoys from Wei came on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以前司空王敬則為太尉。

translations.literal: On jiawu, former Minister of Works Wang Jingze was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, former Minister of Works Wang Jingze was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，復置南蠻校尉官。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the office of Commandant of Southern Barbarians was restored.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the office of Commandant of Southern Barbarians was restored.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，詔使者觀省風俗。

translations.literal: On jiachen, an edict ordered envoys to observe and inspect local customs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, an edict ordered envoys to observe and inspect local customs.

sentences.zh: 九月癸未，誅新除司徒鄱陽王鏘、中軍大將軍隨王子隆。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on guiwei, the newly appointed Grand Tutor Prince of Poyang Qiang and Grand General of the Central Army Prince of Sui Zilong were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month on guiwei, the newly appointed Grand Tutor Prince of Poyang Qiang and Grand General of the Central Army Prince of Sui Zilong were executed.

sentences.zh: 遣平西將軍王廣之誅南兗州刺史安陸王子敬。

translations.literal: Pacifying-West General Wang Guangzhi was dispatched to execute Governor of South Yan Province Prince of Anlu Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-West General Wang Guangzhi was dispatched to execute Governor of South Yan Province Prince of Anlu Zijing.

sentences.zh: 於是江州刺史晉安王子懋起兵，遣中護軍王玄邈討誅之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Governor of Jiang Province Prince of Jin'an Zimao raised troops; Central Guard General Wang Xuanmiao was dispatched to suppress and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Governor of Jiang Province Prince of Jin'an Zimao raised troops; Central Guard General Wang Xuanmiao was dispatched to suppress and execute him.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，又誅湘州刺史南平王銳、郢州刺史晉熙王銶、南豫州刺史宜都王鏗。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Prince of Nanping Rui, Governor of Xiang Province, Prince of Jinyi Chao, Governor of Ying Province, and Prince of Yidu Keng, Governor of South Yu Province, were again executed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Prince of Nanping Rui, Governor of Xiang Province, Prince of Jinyi Chao, Governor of Ying Province, and Prince of Yidu Keng, Governor of South Yu Province, were again executed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以衛將軍廬陵王子卿為司徒，以撫軍將軍桂陽王鑠為中軍將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On dinghai, General of the Guard Prince of Luling Ziqing was made Grand Tutor; General Who Pacifies the Army Prince of Guiyang Shuo was made Grand General of the Central Army with an office opening at ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, General of the Guard Prince of Luling Ziqing was made Grand Tutor; General Who Pacifies the Army Prince of Guiyang Shuo was made Grand General of the Central Army with an office opening at ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁酉，加宣城公鸞黃鉞，進授都督中外諸軍事、太傅，領大將軍、揚州牧，加殊禮，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on dingyou, Duke of Xuancheng Luan was given the yellow axe, promoted to Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, Grand Preceptor, holding Grand General and Governor of Yang Province, with extraordinary honors, promoted to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter on dingyou, Duke of Xuancheng Luan was given the yellow axe, promoted to Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, Grand Preceptor, holding Grand General and Governor of Yang Province, with extraordinary honors, and elevated to prince.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，誅新除中軍將軍桂陽王鑠、撫軍將軍衡陽王鈞、侍中秘書監江夏王鋒、鎮軍將軍建安王子真、左將軍巴陵王子倫。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the newly appointed Grand General of the Central Army Prince of Guiyang Shuo, General Who Pacifies the Army Prince of Hengyang Jun, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Library Prince of Jiangxia Feng, General Who Garrisons the Army Prince of Jian'an Zizhen, and General of the Left Prince of Baling Zilun were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the newly appointed Grand General of the Central Army Prince of Guiyang Shuo, General Who Pacifies the Army Prince of Hengyang Jun, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Library Prince of Jiangxia Feng, General Who Garrisons the Army Prince of Jian'an Zizhen, and General of the Left Prince of Baling Zilun were executed.

sentences.zh: 是時宣城王鸞輔政，帝起居皆諮而後行。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Xuancheng Luan assisted in government; the emperor's comings and goings were all consulted before acting.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Prince of Xuancheng Luan assisted in government; the emperor's comings and goings were all consulted before he acted.

sentences.zh: 思食蒸魚菜，太官令答無錄公命，竟不與。

translations.literal: Wishing to eat steamed fish and vegetables, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen replied that without the Duke's order there was no record — in the end none was given.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to eat steamed fish and vegetables, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen replied that without the Duke's order there was no record — in the end none was given.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，皇太后令廢帝為海陵王，使宣城王入纂皇統。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Empress Dowager issued an order deposing the emperor as Prince of Hailing and ordering Prince of Xuancheng to enter and succeed the imperial line.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Empress Dowager issued an order deposing the emperor as Prince of Hailing and ordering Prince of Xuancheng to enter and succeed the imperial line.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，詔海陵王依漢東海王強故事，給虎賁、旄頭、畫輪車，設鍾簴宮縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, an edict ordered Prince of Hailing to follow the Han precedent of Prince Qiang of Donghai — given tiger guards, plumed headgear, and painted-wheel carriage, with bell stands and palace music established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu, an edict ordered Prince of Hailing to follow the Han precedent of Prince Qiang of Donghai — given tiger guards, plumed headgear, and painted-wheel carriage, with bell stands and palace music established.

sentences.zh: 十一月，稱王有疾，數遣禦師往視，乃殞之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, claiming the prince was ill, imperial physicians were repeatedly sent to examine him — then he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, claiming the prince was ill, imperial physicians were repeatedly sent to examine him — then he was killed.

sentences.zh: 給溫明秘器，斂以袞冕之服，大鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: Warm-bright secret vessels were granted; he was encoffined in robe and crown; the Grand Master of Ceremonies supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Warm-bright secret vessels were granted; he was encoffined in robe and crown; the Grand Master of Ceremonies supervised the funeral.

sentences.zh: 葬給轀輬車，九旒大輅，黃屋左纛，前後部羽葆、鼓吹，輓歌二部，依東海王強故事，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Burial was granted a wheeled bier, the great carriage with nine tassels, yellow canopy and left banner, front and rear feather-canopies and martial pipes and drums, two sets of elegy-singers — following the precedent of Prince Qiang of Donghai; posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Burial was granted a wheeled bier, the great carriage with nine tassels, yellow canopy and left banner, front and rear feather-canopies and martial pipes and drums, and two sets of elegy-singers — following the precedent of Prince Qiang of Donghai; posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 先是武帝立禪靈寺於都下，當世以為壯觀，天意若曰：「禪「者禪也，「靈」者神明之目也，武帝晏駕而鼎業傾移也。

translations.literal: Previously Emperor Wu had built Chanling Temple in the capital — contemporaries considered it magnificent; Heaven's intent seemed to say: "Chan" means abdication, "ling" means the eye of the spirits — Emperor Wu departed and the cauldron enterprise shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Emperor Wu had built Chanling Temple in the capital — contemporaries considered it magnificent; Heaven's intent seemed to say: Chan means abdication, ling means the eye of the spirits — Emperor Wu departed and the imperial enterprise shifted.

sentences.zh: 永明世，市里小兒以鐵相擊於地，謂之「鬥鑿」，「鑿」之為言：「族」也，至是宗室族滅矣。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, market children struck iron on the ground calling it "fighting chisel"; "chisel" as word means "clan" — at this the imperial clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming era, market children struck iron on the ground calling it fighting chisel; chisel as word sounds like clan — at this the imperial clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 又武帝時以燕支為朱衣，朝士皆服之，及明帝以宗子入纂，此又奪朱之效也。

translations.literal: Also in Emperor Wu's time cinnabar paste was used for vermilion robes and court gentlemen all wore them; when Emperor Ming entered as a clansman to succeed, this was again the effect of seizing vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: Also in Emperor Wu's time cinnabar paste was used for vermilion robes and court gentlemen all wore them; when Emperor Ming entered as a clansman to succeed, this was again the omen of seizing vermilion.

sentences.zh: 時又多以生紗為帽，半其裙而析之，號曰：「倚勸」。

translations.literal: At that time many also used raw gauze for caps, halving the skirt and splitting it, called "leaning exhortation."
translations.idiomatic: At that time many also used raw gauze for caps, halving the skirt and splitting it, called leaning exhortation.

sentences.zh: 先是人間語好云：「擾攘建武」，至是朝士勸進，實為匆遽，「倚勸」「擾攘」之言，於是驗矣。

translations.literal: Previously among the people the saying was favored: "turmoil Jianwu" — at this court gentlemen urged advancement, truly in haste; the words "leaning exhortation" and "turmoil" were here verified.
translations.idiomatic: Previously among the people the favored saying was turmoil Jianwu — at this court gentlemen urged advancement in true haste; the words leaning exhortation and turmoil were here verified.

sentences.zh: 高宗明皇帝

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, the High Ancestor
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, the High Ancestor

sentences.zh: 海陵王立，為驃騎大將軍、錄尚書事、揚州刺史，加都督，增班劍為三十人，封宣城郡公，鎮東府城，給兵五千人，錢二百萬，布千匹。

translations.literal: When Prince of Hailing was installed, he was made Rapid Cavalry General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Governor of Yang Province, with added command; ceremonial swords increased to thirty men; enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng Commandery; garrisoned Eastern Headquarters city; given five thousand troops, two million cash, and a thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Hailing was installed, he was made Rapid Cavalry General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yang Province, with added command; ceremonial swords increased to thirty men; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng Commandery, garrisoned Eastern Headquarters city, and given five thousand troops, two million cash, and a thousand bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 九江事難，假黃鉞，事寧，表送之。

translations.literal: When the Jiujiang affair was difficult, the yellow axe was lent; when affairs settled, he memorialized to return it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiujiang affair grew difficult, the yellow axe was lent; when affairs settled, he memorialized to return it.

sentences.zh: 尋加黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事、太傅，領大將軍、揚州牧，增班劍為四十人，給幢絡三望車，前後部羽葆、鼓吹，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎、掾、屬各四人，封宣城王。

translations.literal: Soon the yellow axe was added, with command of all military affairs within and without, Grand Preceptor, holding Grand General and Governor of Yang Province; ceremonial swords increased to forty men; given canopy-banners and three-canopy carriage, front and rear feather-canopies and martial pipes and drums, sword at court and shoes in hall, no hurrying at audience, no naming at obeisance; left and right senior clerks, marshals, attendants, aides and subordinates four each; enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the yellow axe was added, with command of all military affairs within and without, Grand Preceptor, holding Grand General and Governor of Yang Province; ceremonial swords increased to forty men; he was given canopy-banners and a three-canopy carriage, front and rear feather-canopies and martial pipes and drums, sword at court and shoes in hall, no hurrying at audience, no naming at obeisance; left and right senior clerks, marshals, attendants, aides and subordinates four each; and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 未拜，太后令廢海陵王，以上入纂高帝為第三子，群臣三請，乃受命。

translations.literal: Before accepting office, the Empress Dowager ordered Prince of Hailing deposed and the emperor to enter and succeed as Emperor Gao's third son; the officials thrice requested — then he accepted mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Before accepting office, the Empress Dowager ordered Prince of Hailing deposed and the emperor to enter and succeed as Emperor Gao's third son; the officials thrice requested — then he accepted the mandate.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬申，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on renshen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month on renshen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 帝宿沐浴，不禦內。

translations.literal: The emperor lodged, bathed, and did not enter the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lodged, bathed, and did not enter the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 其日，潔齋蔬食，斷朝務，屏人，單衣帢危坐，以至事畢。

translations.literal: That day he kept pure fast with vegetable food, suspended court affairs, dismissed attendants, sat alone in single garment and kerchief until affairs were complete.
translations.idiomatic: That day he kept pure fast with vegetable food, suspended court affairs, dismissed attendants, and sat alone in single garment and kerchief until affairs were complete.

sentences.zh: 追尊始安貞王為景皇，妃江氏為懿後，別立寢廟，號陵曰修安。

translations.literal: Prince of Shi'an Zhen was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing; Consort Jiang as Empress Yi; a separate sleeping temple was established; the tomb was named Xiuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shi'an Zhen was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing; Consort Jiang as Empress Yi; a separate ancestral temple was established; the tomb was named Xiuan.

sentences.zh: 封桂陽王鑠等諸王子皆為列侯。

translations.literal: The sons of Prince of Guiyang Shuo and other princes were all enfeoffed as ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Prince of Guiyang Shuo and other princes were all enfeoffed as ranked marquises.

sentences.zh: 凡諸王侯得罪者，諸子皆復屬籍。

translations.literal: For all princes and marquises who had offended, their sons were all restored to the register.
translations.idiomatic: For all princes and marquises who had offended, their sons were all restored to the register.

sentences.zh: 又詔遣大使觀省四方。

translations.literal: Also an edict dispatched grand envoys to observe and inspect the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also dispatched grand envoys to observe and inspect the four directions.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，革永明之制，依晉、宋舊典，太子以師禮敬少傅。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Yongming's regulations were reformed to follow Jin and Song old statutes; the crown prince with master's rites honored the Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Yongming's regulations were reformed to follow Jin and Song old statutes; the crown prince with master's rites honored the Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，進大司馬尋陽公王敬則等十三人爵邑各有差。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Grand Marshal Duke of Xunyang Wang Jingze and twelve others were promoted in rank and fief with graded differences.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Grand Marshal Duke of Xunyang Wang Jingze and twelve others were promoted in rank and fief with graded differences.

sentences.zh: 省新林苑，先是百姓地者，悉以還主。

translations.literal: Xinlin Park was abolished; where it had been common people's land, all was returned to owners.
translations.idiomatic: Xinlin Park was abolished; where it had been common people's land, all was returned to the owners.

sentences.zh: 廢南蠻校尉官。

translations.literal: The office of Commandant of Southern Barbarians was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The office of Commandant of Southern Barbarians was abolished.

sentences.zh: 己卯，追崇妃劉氏為敬皇后，號陵曰興安。

translations.literal: On jimao, Consort Liu was posthumously honored as Empress Jing; the tomb was named Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Consort Liu was posthumously honored as Empress Jing; the tomb was named Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，立皇子寶義為晉安王，寶玄為江夏王，寶源為廬陵王，寶寅為建安王，寶融為隨郡王，寶攸為南平王。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Prince Baoqi was installed as Prince of Jin'an, Baoquan as Prince of Jiangxia, Baoyuan as Prince of Luling, Baoyin as Prince of Jian'an, Baorong as Prince of Sui Commandery, and Baoyou as Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Prince Baoqi was installed as Prince of Jin'an, Baoquan as Prince of Jiangxia, Baoyuan as Prince of Luling, Baoyin as Prince of Jian'an, Baorong as Prince of Sui Commandery, and Baoyou as Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 甲申，斷官長貢獻及私餉遺。

translations.literal: On jiashen, official chiefs' tribute and private gifts were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, official chiefs' tribute and private gifts were cut off.

sentences.zh: 以安陸昭王緬第二子寶晊襲封安陸王。

translations.literal: Prince Baoqi, second son of Prince of Anlu Mian, succeeded as Prince of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Baoqi, second son of Prince of Anlu Mian, succeeded as Prince of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔細作、中署、材官、車府，凡諸工可悉開番假，遞令休息。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict ordered fine crafts, central workshops, materiel officers and carriage offices — all craftsmen could open rotating leave and rest in turn.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, an edict ordered fine crafts, central workshops, materiel officers and carriage offices — all craftsmen could open rotating leave and rest in turn.

sentences.zh: 戊子，立皇子寶卷為皇太子，賜天下為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Prince Baoquan was installed as crown prince; all who were fathers of heirs received one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Prince Baoquan was installed as crown prince; all who were fathers of heirs received one rank of nobility.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔東宮肇建，遠近或有慶禮，可悉斷之。

translations.literal: On jichou, an edict: as the Eastern Palace was newly built, congratulatory gifts from near and far, if any, were all cut off.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, an edict: as the Eastern Palace was newly built, congratulatory gifts from near and far, if any, were all cut off.

sentences.zh: 永明中，御史中丞沈深表：百官年登七十者，皆令致仕，並窮困私門。

translations.literal: In Yongming, Censor-in-Chief Shen Shen memorialized: officials reaching seventy were all ordered to retire and confined to private poverty.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming, Censor-in-Chief Shen Shen memorialized: officials reaching seventy were all ordered to retire and confined to private poverty.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔「自縉紳年及，可一遵永明七年以前銓敘之科」。

translations.literal: On gengzi, an edict: "From gentry and officials reaching age, uniformly follow the selection standards before the seventh year of Yongming."
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, an edict: "From gentry and officials reaching age, uniformly follow the selection standards before the seventh year of Yongming."

sentences.zh: 十二月庚戌，宣德太僕劉朗之、遊擊將軍劉璩之子，坐不贍給兄子，致使隨母他嫁，免官，禁錮終身，付之鄉論。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on gengxu, Grand Master of Imperial Stud Liu Langzhi and son of Mobile Corps General Liu Qu — for not supporting a nephew, causing him to follow his mother in remarriage — were dismissed, forbidden for life, and handed to local judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month on gengxu, Grand Master of Imperial Stud Liu Langzhi and son of Mobile Corps General Liu Qu — for not supporting a nephew, causing him to follow his mother in remarriage — were dismissed, forbidden from office for life, and handed to local judgment.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏孝文皇帝遷都洛陽。

translations.literal: That year, Emperor Xiaowen of Wei moved the capital to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Emperor Xiaowen of Wei moved the capital to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月辛未，降都下系囚殊死以下。

translations.literal: In the second year, first month on xinwei, capital prisoners below extraordinary death were reduced in sentence.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, first month on xinwei, capital prisoners below extraordinary death were reduced in sentence.

sentences.zh: 詔王公以下各舉所知，內外群僚各進忠言，無有所諱。

translations.literal: An edict: princes and officials down should each recommend those known; inner and outer officials should each advance loyal words without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict: princes and officials down should each recommend those they knew; inner and outer officials should each advance loyal words without concealment.

sentences.zh: 魏攻豫、司、徐、梁四州。

translations.literal: Wei attacked Yu, Si, Xu and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Wei attacked Yu, Si, Xu and Liang provinces.

sentences.zh: 壬申，遣鎮南將軍王廣之督司州，右衛將軍蕭坦之督徐州，尚書右僕射沈文季督豫州，以拒魏。

translations.literal: On renshen, General Who Garrisons the South Wang Guangzhi was dispatched to command Si Province; General of the Right Guard Xiao Tanzhi to command Xu Province; Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Wenji to command Yu Province — to resist Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, General Who Garrisons the South Wang Guangzhi was dispatched to command Si Province; General of the Right Guard Xiao Tanzhi to command Xu Province; Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Wenji to command Yu Province — to resist Wei.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔都下二縣，有毀發墳壟，隨宜修理。

translations.literal: On jimao, an edict: in the two capital counties, where graves were opened and violated, repair as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, an edict: in the two capital counties, where graves were opened and violated, repair as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 乙未，魏軍攻鍾離，徐州刺史蕭惠休破之。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Wei army attacked Zhongli; Governor of Xu Province Xiao Huiqiu defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the Wei army attacked Zhongli; Governor of Xu Province Xiao Huiqiu defeated them.

sentences.zh: 丙申，加太尉陳顯達使持節、都督西北道諸軍事。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Grand Commandant Chen Xianda was given acting authority and command of northwest-route military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Grand Commandant Chen Xianda was given acting authority and command of northwest-route military affairs.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，內外纂嚴。

translations.literal: On dingyou, inner and outer quarters were placed under strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, inner and outer quarters were placed under strict guard.

sentences.zh: 二月己未，司州刺史蕭誕與眾軍攻敗魏軍。

translations.literal: In the second month on jiwei, Governor of Si Province Xiao Yan with the mass of armies defeated the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month on jiwei, Governor of Si Province Xiao Yan with the mass of armies defeated the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 詔雍、豫、司、南兗、徐五州遭遇兵戎之家，悉停今年稅調。

translations.literal: An edict: in Yong, Yu, Si, South Yan and Xu provinces, households encountering military affairs — all this year's taxes and levies were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict: in Yong, Yu, Si, South Yan and Xu provinces, households encountering military affairs — all that year's taxes and levies were stopped.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，停青州麥租。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Qing Province wheat rent was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Qing Province wheat rent was stopped.

sentences.zh: 魏軍自壽春退。

translations.literal: The Wei army withdrew from Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army withdrew from Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 三月甲申，解嚴。

translations.literal: In the third month on jiashen, strict guard was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month on jiashen, strict guard was lifted.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己亥朔，親錄三百里內獄訟，自外委州郡訊察，三署徒隸，原遣有差。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on the first day, jihai, the emperor personally recorded lawsuits within three hundred li; beyond, entrusted to provinces and commanderies for investigation; convict laborers of the three offices were pardoned and released with graded differences.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer on the first day, jihai, the emperor personally heard lawsuits within three hundred li; beyond that, investigation was entrusted to provinces and commanderies; convict laborers of the three offices were pardoned and released with graded differences.

sentences.zh: 魏軍圍漢中，梁州刺史蕭懿拒退之。

translations.literal: The Wei army besieged Hanzhong; Governor of Liang Province Xiao Yi resisted and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army besieged Hanzhong; Governor of Liang Province Xiao Yi resisted and repelled them.

sentences.zh: 五月甲午，寢廟成，詔監作長帥賜位一等。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on jiawu, when the sleeping temple was complete, an edict granted supervising craftsmen and commanders one rank higher.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month on jiawu, when the sleeping temple was complete, an edict granted supervising craftsmen and commanders one rank higher.

sentences.zh: 六月壬戌，誅領軍蕭諶、西陽王子明、南海王子罕、邵陵王子貞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on renxu, Commandant of the Guards Xiao Chen, Prince of Xiyang Ziming, Prince of Nanhai Zihan and Prince of Shaoling Zizhen were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month on renxu, Commandant of the Guards Xiao Chen, Prince of Xiyang Ziming, Prince of Nanhai Zihan and Prince of Shaoling Zizhen were executed.

sentences.zh: 秋九月己丑，改封南平王寶攸為邵陵王，蜀郡王子文為西陽王，廣漢王子峻為衡陽王，臨海王昭秀為巴陵王，永嘉王昭粲為桂陽王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn on jichou, Prince of Nanping Baoyou was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling, Prince of Shu Commandery Ziwen as Prince of Xiyang, Prince of Guanghan Zijun as Prince of Hengyang, Prince of Linhai Zhaoxiu as Prince of Baling, and Prince of Yongjia Zhaocan as Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn on jichou, Prince of Nanping Baoyou was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling, Prince of Shu Commandery Ziwen as Prince of Xiyang, Prince of Guanghan Zijun as Prince of Hengyang, Prince of Linhai Zhaoxiu as Prince of Baling, and Prince of Yongjia Zhaocan as Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸卯，詔罷東田，毀興光樓，並詔水衡量省禦乘。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on guimao, an edict abolished Eastern Field and destroyed Xingguang Tower; also an edict measured water and reduced imperial carriages.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter on guimao, an edict abolished Eastern Field and destroyed Xingguang Tower; also an edict measured water levels and reduced imperial carriages.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，納皇太子妃褚氏，大赦，王公以下班賜各有差，斷四方上禮。

translations.literal: On yimao, the crown prince's consort of the Chu clan was received; general amnesty; princes and officials down received graded gifts; tribute from the four directions was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the crown prince's consort of the Chu clan was received; general amnesty; princes and officials down received graded gifts; tribute from the four directions was cut off.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁酉，詔晉帝諸陵，悉皆修理，並增守衛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on dingyou, an edict: Jin emperors' tombs were all repaired and guards increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month on dingyou, an edict: Jin emperors' tombs were all repaired and guards increased.

sentences.zh: 吳、晉陵失稔之鄉，蠲三調有差。

translations.literal: In Wu and Jinling districts of failed harvest, the three levies were remitted with graded differences.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu and Jinling districts of failed harvest, the three levies were remitted with graded differences.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丁卯，以陰平王楊炅子崇祖為沙州刺史，封陰平王。

translations.literal: In the third year, first month on dingmao, Prince Yang Jiong's son Chongzu was made Governor of Sha Province and enfeoffed as Prince of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, first month on dingmao, Prince Yang Jiong's son Chongzu was made Governor of Sha Province and enfeoffed as Prince of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔申明守長六周之制，事竟不行。

translations.idiomatic: On wushen, an edict increased Confucius's sacrificial rank.

translations.idiomatic: Great affairs are to be consulted with Shen Wenji, Jiang Si and Liu Xuan.

translations.idiomatic: Confidant responsibilities may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Huiqiu and Cui Huijing.

translations.idiomatic: "The officials submitted posthumous title Emperor Ming, temple name High Ancestor; burial at Xing'an Tomb.

translations.literal: The emperor was clear-sighted with administrative talent; in holding law he showed no favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was clear-sighted with administrative talent; in holding to the law he showed no favor.

translations.literal: He regulated imperial favorites; officials below were purified.
translations.idiomatic: He regulated imperial favorites; officials below were kept in order.

translations.literal: He employed poor men — four-canopy umbrellas could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: He employed poor men — four-canopy umbrellas could not be used.

translations.idiomatic: Greatly preserving frugality, he abolished the Xinlin Park that Emperor Wu had built and returned the land to the people.

translations.idiomatic: He abolished Eastern Field that Crown Prince Wenhu had built and sold it off.

translations.idiomatic: In Yongming, carriages, litters and boats — all gold and silver was stripped and returned to the robe treasury; ivory and horn substituted.

translations.idiomatic: By nature suspicious, he frequently executed.

translations.idiomatic: He practiced channel arts and used numerology.

translations.idiomatic: Whenever going out on tour, he first divined benefit and harm.

translations.idiomatic: He wore deep-red robes; clothing and ornaments were all red, as counter-magic.

translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor Marquess of Donghun

translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, seventh month on jiyou, Emperor Ming died; the crown prince ascended the throne.

translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter on jiwei, an edict reduced and simplified legal statutes.
